talks.title: Reversing Corruption in Seagate HDD
talks.summary:
In this presentation at the DEF CON 27 Hardware Hacking Village, Allison Naaktgeboren details the reverse engineering and recovery process for corrupted translator firmware in modern Seagate hard disk drives. She begins at 04:00 by explaining the physical architecture and failure modes of magnetic media drives, where microcode corruption can trigger the dreaded "busy bug" (BSY status) and prevent drives from identifying LBAs to the host controller. She estimates the widespread scale of this issue at 08:00, noting that among tens of millions of deployed drives, translator table corruption accounts for a substantial fraction of seemingly dead units.

At 12:00, Allison breaks down the mechanics of the translator subsystem, which maps Logical Block Addresses (LBAs) used by operating systems to Physical Block Addresses (PBAs) on the platters while taking into account factory defect tables (P-List) and reallocated bad sectors (G-List). She demonstrates connecting to the drive's onboard serial UART interface at 16:00 to issue low-level diagnostic commands and inspect firmware error logs. She then walks through the disassembly of the proprietary translator data structures at 20:00, highlighting the intricacies of recovering grown defect entries at 24:00.

Finally, Allison unveils an open-source Python recovery tool suite at 28:00, designed to automate parsing and rebuilding corrupted Seagate translator tables without requiring expensive proprietary hardware like PC-3000. She wraps up at 32:00 by warning researchers about electrical and mechanical hazards when servicing sensitive drive electronics, providing guidance for data recovery practitioners and hardware researchers.
